title: Plant Order-Entry Standard: Build Class Placement and the Committed Ship Date (Factory Production Orders)
content:
**Standard.** An order takes the highest-ranked build class whose listed features it contains; for example a wood-clad order with laminated glass is an Architectural Wood Build, and a vinyl order with a single arched unit is a Specialty Shape Build. The order is entered within the stated business days after the contract's order release. The committed ship date is the order entry date plus the class standard lead time, plus the class large-order extension when the unit count exceeds the class large-order threshold, counted in business days (Monday through Friday, excluding U.S. federal holidays) starting the day after entry. The committed ship date is printed on the acknowledgment and never changes; later delays move only the current ship date. An order may not carry more units than the class maximum; a larger contract is split by the factory into consecutive orders only by engineering approval, which support cannot grant.

This standard governs all Factory Production Orders. The class features, ranks, unit maximums, standard lead times, large-order thresholds and extensions, and the order-entry period are the figures of each build class.

## The committed lead, broken down

1. The committed lead starts from the class standard lead time.
2. When the order's unit count is greater than the class large-order threshold, the class large-order extension is added to it; at or below the threshold, nothing is added.
3. The committed ship date is the business day reached by counting the committed lead in business days, starting the day after the order entry date.

## Worked example (hypothetical order, no federal holiday in the period)

A Custom Size Build order of 21 units is entered on a Monday. The class standard lead time is 20 business days and the large-order threshold is 20 units; 21 units exceed it, so the 5-business-day extension is added and the committed lead is 25 business days. Counting starts on the Tuesday; the 25th business day is the Monday five weeks after entry, which is the committed ship date. The same order with 20 units would have a committed lead of 20 business days and a committed ship date on the Monday four weeks after entry.

## Points of judgement

- **Committed versus current date.** The committed ship date printed on the acknowledgment stays fixed for the life of the order; a delay changes only the current ship date.
- **Unit maximum.** An order over the class maximum is not entered as one order; only engineering approval splits a larger contract into consecutive orders, and support cannot grant that approval.
